fr:title.text: Repurposing old hardware in the homelab

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Repurposing old hardware in the homelab

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Brainstorm: what can I do with the Pixel 6, possibly other retired phones, and a Surface Book 2 with a degrading battery? The existing homelab is macproseph (NixOS, Tailscale-only) plus schmapple (laptop) and nixos — see the flake description in ~/nix-config. I want more devices to tinker with, not more devices to babysit.

html:ul.html:li: No batteries in service. Swollen LiPo cells are a fire risk and a dying battery makes uptime nondeterministic. Anything I redeploy should run off a wall adapter, with the internal cell either removed, bypassed, or ignored (plugged in permanently and let it age out).

NixOS where possible. The whole homelab is managed declaratively from ~/nix-config. A new node that can't join that flake is a new snowflake to maintain — acceptable only if the device buys something I can't get elsewhere.
Small surface area. Each reuse should be a weekend-scale project with a clear "done" state, not an open-ended research program.

Pixel 6 (Tensor G1, ARM64). Bootloader is OEM-unlockable. Options: postmarketOS (Alpine, mature tablet/phone support), Mobile NixOS (experimental but declarative, matches the rest of the fleet), or stock AOSP running a Linux chroot. Battery is fine today but will swell; plan to run it with the back opened and the cell disconnected or replaced by a dummy.

Surface Book 2 (x86_64, dGPU in the keyboard base, battery degraded). NixOS support is good — the nixos-hardware repo has a microsoft/surface module, and linux-surface kernel patches are packaged. The dGPU is the interesting bit; the dead battery is not a blocker if the machine lives on a shelf.
Other old phones (TBD). Depends on what's actually in the drawer — likely a mix of older Pixels / Samsungs with varying postmarketOS support.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Rough ranking by tinker value ÷ maintenance cost, not commitment. Anything I actually pursue spawns its own TODO and (if it grows) a milestone.

html:ul.html:li: Wall-mounted dashboard (phone). USB-powered kiosk showing the forest dashboard, Grafana, or a calendar. Minimal software — a locked-down browser pointed at a Tailscale URL. The phone's built-in screen + touch is the whole appeal; no battery needed once it's on a charger behind the frame.

Surface Book 2 as a second server. Shelf-mounted, lid closed, battery disconnected or ignored. Joins the flake as a third NixOS host; picks up workloads that macproseph doesn't want — LLM inference on the dGPU, heavier CI, occasional GUI via RDP / Sunshine.

Pixel 6 on postmarketOS as an ARM test node. A tiny always-on ARM64 machine for cross-compilation targets, Tailscale exit node experiments, or a secondary DNS / ad-block resolver. Declarative config story is weak unless Mobile NixOS works well enough for this device.

Phone as a security / doorbell camera. RTSP streamer feeding a Frigate instance on macproseph. Uses the camera, a hardware asset that's otherwise wasted. Battery removal is non-negotiable here — these live on 24/7.

Phone as a physical-button / NFC trigger. Mounted near the desk, running a minimal service that hits the capture endpoint or toggles home-automation scenes when tapped. Low-stakes way to learn postmarketOS.

Surface Book 2 as a homemade Steam Deck. The screen half is effectively a self-contained tablet; strip off the keyboard base, run SteamOS (or NixOS with steam + Gamescope session), and treat the result as a couch/handheld gaming device. This is the one candidate that violates the no-batteries rule — a handheld without a battery isn't a handheld — so the SB2's tablet cell has to be kept in service, which means accepting the failure mode and swapping the cell when it swells. Competes with the "second server" use; only one of the two survives.
How mature is Mobile NixOS on Tensor G1 as of April 2026? If it's broken, postmarketOS + nix package manager is the fallback, but that loses declarative OS config.

Is it practical to power a Pixel 6 indefinitely with the battery removed, or does the power-management IC refuse to boot without a cell present? (Some phones need a fake battery resistor; some don't.)
Surface Book 2: can the screen half be used independently from the keyboard base (it has its own CPU/RAM/battery), or does the interesting compute all live in the base?
